binders: There exists a real constant c.
Universally quantify over a finite type ι and a measurable space Ω.
Universally quantify over a measure μ on Ω equipped with the assertion that μ is a probability measure.
Universally quantify over a family X : ι → Ω → Real, together with evidence that the full finite index set is nonempty.
Universally quantify over a real threshold t.
hypotheses: The finite index type is nonempty.
For every i, X i is Borel-measurable.
For every i, X i is μ-integrable and has integral zero.
For every i, LocalDef001 μ (X i) is strictly below infinity in ENNReal.
The family X is mutually independent under μ.
conclusions: Let N = card(ι), K = max_i (LocalDef001 μ (X i)).toReal, and A(ω) = (1/N) ∑_i X i ω. Then μ.real({ω | |A(ω)| ≥ t}) ≤ 2 exp(-c N min(t²/K², t/K)).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef002 μ X s means that X is measurable, s is an ENNReal scale distinct from 0 and infinity, exp(|X|/s.toReal) is μ-integrable, and its μ-integral is at most 2.
LocalDef001 μ X is the ENNReal infimum of all scales s satisfying LocalDef002 μ X s.
N is the positive natural cardinality of the nonempty finite index type, cast to Real where it appears in arithmetic.
K is the nonempty finite maximum of the real conversions of the LocalDef001 scales.
A is the arithmetic average of the family: every X i has coefficient 1/N.
The measured event is the inclusive two-sided tail event {|A| ≥ t}.
The exponential decay rate is cN times the minimum of the quadratic regime t²/K² and the linear regime t/K.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is one universal positive real constant c such that, for every nonempty finite family of mutually independent, measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables with finite exponential-moment scales, the probability that the absolute value of their arithmetic average is at least any nonnegative threshold t is at most twice exp(-c times the family size times the minimum of t squared divided by the square of the largest scale and t divided by that largest scale).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The witness c is chosen before the index type, probability space, measure, family, and threshold, so it is uniform over all such data.
The index type must be finite and nonempty. Consequently N = card(ι) is positive, and the averaging factor 1/N does not divide by zero.
All summands have exactly the same coefficient 1/N; the proposition is about the arithmetic average, not an arbitrary weighted sum.
The variables need not be identically distributed; mutual independence, individual regularity, zero means, and finite scales are the only family conditions.
There is no explicit positivity hypothesis on K. Even though every admissible scale is individually nonzero, the infimum LocalDef001 can be zero, for example as a limiting infimum.

Real division is totalized, so if K = 0 then both t²/K² and t/K are defined by Lean arithmetic rather than being undefined. With real inverse zero equal to zero, both quotients evaluate to zero and the right side becomes 2.
At t = 0 the inclusive event is the whole sample space. If K > 0, both rate branches are ordinarily zero; if K = 0, Lean additionally totalizes the resulting zero denominators.
The finiteness assumptions LocalDef001 < infinity ensure that the subsequent ENNReal.toReal conversions do not receive infinity.
LocalDef001 is an infimum; the proposition does not assert that an admissible scale attaining the infimum exists.

If the admissible-scale set has exceptional behavior such as being empty, its value is governed by the supplied complete-order infimum semantics; the dossier does not separately characterize that case.
The left side uses Measure.real, converting the event's ENNReal measure to Real. The probability-measure hypothesis supplies the intended finite probability interpretation.
The event uses a non-strict threshold ≥ and is two-sided because of the absolute value.
The exponential-moment scale uses the exact threshold 2 and requires integrability of the exponential, not merely a pointwise or almost-everywhere bound.
ambiguities: The dossier supplies the scale only through the anonymous definitions LocalDef001 and LocalDef002; describing it as an Orlicz or sub-exponential scale is an interpretation of the explicit infimum formula, not an additional identity.
No norm axioms, scaling law, or infimum-attainment theorem for LocalDef001 is included.
The dossier does not independently characterize when LocalDef001 equals zero or when the admissible-scale set is empty.
ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun is interpreted from its supplied definition as mutual independence of the indexed functions under μ.
The target does not state a preferred numerical value for the universal constant c.
